label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Posting this so other Vegas planners have a recent experience to consider before booking Sunbelt Charter Coaches for CES season, especially for larger groups.

On Thursday, November 5, I booked Sunbelt to transport 220 guests from a hotel to a client dinner at a ranch venue in Henderson. We contracted for four coaches with a 6:15 p.m. pickup. The booking was confirmed in writing twice, most recently on Tuesday, November 3. We paid the full $8,400: a 50% deposit in September and the balance seven days before the event.

Only two of the four coaches showed up. The first arrived 55 minutes late. That driver told me he had received the assignment at 5 p.m. The second coach broke down on the 215 with its AC not working, leaving guests on the shoulder for approximately 40 minutes.

With no backup transportation provided, I put 60 guests into Ubers and Lyfts on my company card, at a cost of approximately $1,900. Dinner began at 8:40 p.m. instead of 7 p.m., and the caterer charged overtime.

Corey was the dispatcher listed on our booking communications. Since Friday, my calls to the office line have gone to voicemail, and I have not received a resolution to my refund request. I’m asking for a refund for the two coaches that never arrived, plus reimbursement for the rideshare costs.

For context, Sunbelt handled two smaller airport runs for us last spring and did a great job. That experience is why I trusted them with this dinner. A late bus is something I can work around. Two missing coaches, a breakdown, and no backup plan or adequate communication are a different situation.

My client is now reviewing whether to retain us for their March event. I can’t say how that decision will land, but this transportation failure has put the relationship at risk.

Based on this experience, I would not book Sunbelt for a large event unless they can demonstrate that they’ve addressed dispatch, backup coverage, and communication when something goes wrong.
